Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above?

I. ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)=1$

II. ${lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)=0$

III. ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)$
question.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. As $x$ approaches $-1,$ the function $f(x)$ approaches the value $y=1.$ Consequently, 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)=1.
$$

- Statement II is true. As $x$ approaches $0,$ the function $f(x)$ approaches the value $y=0.$ Consequently, 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)=0.
$$

- Statement III is false. As $x$ approaches $1,$ the function $f(x)$ approaches the value $y=1,$ and consequently 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=1.
$$

 
Similarly, as $x$ approaches $2,$ the function $f(x)$ approaches the value $y=0,$ and consequently, 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)=0.
$$

 As a result,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x).
$$

In conclusion, only statements I and II are true.
